title: Geographic Flight Routes with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that renders a 3D globe with animated flight routes and a toggleable physics debug overlay.

## Scene Setup
- Create a sphere (radius 5) representing Earth with a blue (#1a4d8f) material and wireframe overlay (green, #00ff44, opacity 0.15).
- Position the camera at (0, 0, 18) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (10, 10, 10) with intensity 0.8.
- Use OrbitControls for camera interaction.

## Flight Routes
- Define exactly 5 flight routes as great-circle arcs on the globe surface, each represented as a curved tube (TubeGeometry, radius 0.03):
  - Route 0: NYC (40.7N, 74.0W) to London (51.5N, 0.1W) — color #ff4444
  - Route 1: London (51.5N, 0.1W) to Dubai (25.3N, 55.3E) — color #44ff44
  - Route 2: Tokyo (35.7N, 139.7E) to Sydney (33.9S, 151.2E) — color #4444ff
  - Route 3: LA (34.1N, 118.2W) to Tokyo (35.7N, 139.7E) — color #ffff44
  - Route 4: Dubai (25.3N, 55.3E) to Sydney (33.9S, 151.2E) — color #ff44ff
- Convert lat/lon to 3D coordinates on the sphere surface. Great-circle arcs should rise above the surface with a peak altitude of radius+0.8 at the midpoint.
- Each route has an animated plane marker (small cone, height 0.3) that travels along the arc. All planes start at t=0 (departure city) and animate to t=1 over 8 seconds, then loop.

## City Markers
- Place small sphere markers (radius 0.12, color #ffffff) at each unique city location on the globe surface. There should be exactly 6 unique cities.

## Physics Debug Overlay
- Implement a debug overlay toggled by pressing 'D'. When active:
  - Show velocity vectors for each plane as ArrowHelper (yellow, length proportional to speed, scale factor 2.0).
  - Show a translucent bounding sphere (wireframe, color #ff8800, opacity 0.3) around each plane marker with radius 0.5.
  - Display gravitational acceleration vectors pointing from each plane toward globe center as ArrowHelper (red, length=1.0).
- The debug overlay objects should be added to/removed from the scene (not just visibility toggled).

## Route Selection
- Clicking on a route tube or plane marker selects that route. Selected route should have emissive color set to #ffffff (emissive intensity 0.5). Only one route can be selected at a time. Clicking empty space deselects.
- Pressing number keys 1-5 selects routes 0-4 directly.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Add a top-left HUD panel (id='hud-panel') showing:
  - Total routes: 5
  - Active planes: count of planes currently animating
  - Selected route: index or 'None'
  - Debug mode: ON/OFF
  - Simulation speed: current multiplier
- Add a speed control: pressing '+' increases simulation speed by 0.5x (max 4.0x), pressing '-' decreases by 0.5x (min 0.5x). Default is 1.0x.
- Add a 'Pause' button (id='pause-btn') that toggles animation pause. When paused, planes freeze at current t values.

## Globe Rotation
- Pressing 'R' toggles auto-rotation of the globe (and all children) around Y-axis at 0.005 rad/frame. Default: OFF.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
  - globeRadius: 5
  - routeCount: number of routes (5)
  - cityCount: number of unique city markers (6)
  - planePositions: array of 5 objects {x, y, z, t} for each plane (t is 0-1 progress)
  - selectedRoute: index (0-4) or -1 for none
  - debugMode: boolean
  - simulationSpeed: number
  - isPaused: boolean
  - autoRotate: boolean
  - debugObjectCount: number of debug overlay objects currently in scene
  - planeVelocities: array of 5 numbers (magnitude of velocity for each plane)
  - frameCount: incrementing integer each animation frame
- Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.
physics_constraints: Planes must remain on great-circle arc paths at correct altitude (globe radius + arc height). Velocity vectors must be tangent to the arc path. All plane positions must satisfy: distance from origin is between globeRadius and globeRadius+1.0. Gravitational vectors must point toward origin. Conservation: total number of planes must always be 5. No NaN in any position or velocity.
